sec: The seven findings that matter most
claim: Robinson was not identified by investigators. Sworn testimony establishes that law enforcement did not know the shooter's identity until he surrendered; the surveillance footage alone was insufficient. The case begins with a family recognising a photograph, not with detection. (§6)

sec: The seven findings that matter most
claim: The forensic record naming him is large in volume and narrow in what it can bear. Both laboratories' analysts agreed — unqualified and unrebutted by anyone — that neither can say what action deposited any DNA, or when. That is the single most consistent proposition in the entire body of evidence. (§8.4)

sec: The seven findings that matter most
claim: The strongest-sounding numbers are the most constrained. "At least one trillion" is a reporting cap, not a measurement; only the 6.28 billion figure is an actual reported value. The trigger swab was taken together with the trigger guard, among at least four contributors, with the major profile the most degraded. And five of the seven number-to-location mappings rest on one non-expert witness reading aloud from an exhibit this library has never read. (§8.2)

sec: The seven findings that matter most
claim: The characteristic public error is identifiable and predictable: the transposed conditional — restating a conditional likelihood ratio as the probability that a named person is the source. Four FBI/DOJ reporting limits were put to the FBI examiner and confirmed followed by her; the constraint broke downstream. (§8.4)

The event. A TPUSA event at Utah Valley University, "the first in a series of similar events to be held at college campuses nationwide"; several hundred attended; Kirk was seated under a portable canopy taking questions. "Approximately fifteen minutes into the event, Mr. Kirk was answering a question about mass shootings by transgender individuals when a gunshot rang out."

The great-risk-of-death theory, in the State's own words. Team members "very close to him on his right and left, as well as some behind his canopy"; the crowd surrounding on three sides; temporary fencing separating attendees "by only a matter of feet"; the Hall of Flags directly above and behind; people in the walkway. And decisively: "The bullet's trajectory passed closely to several other individuals beside Mr. Kirk, including the questioner who was standing directly in front of Mr. Kirk." "Children were visible near Mr. Kirk's stage when he was shot."
The surveillance reconstruction — where the charging documents' own narrative starts. Entry to campus about 11:51 a.m. (the affidavit: "approximately 1150 hours");

The rifle. Recovered in a wooded area, wrapped in a towel, containing one spent and three unspent rounds — "no shell casings were found on the roof, suggesting a bolt-action rather than an auto-loading weapon, and only a single round was fired."

The DNA allegation, verbatim. "DNA consistent with Robinson's was found on the trigger, other parts of the rifle, the fired cartridge casing, two of the three unfired cartridges, and the towel."  §8 below is largely an account of the distance between this sentence and the laboratory record.

The note and the messages. A handwritten note under Robinson's keyboard, found by the roommate at Robinson's direction ("look under my keyboard"), of which police found a photograph; and a subsequent text exchange quoted at length, including "I had enough of his hatred. Some hate can't be negotiated out.", "delete this exchange", "Im gonna turn myself in willingly", "you are all I worry about love", and "if any police ask you questions ask for a lawyer and stay silent."
The residence search. "a shell casing with etchings like the etchings found on the shells in the rifle near UVU", and "several targets with bullet holes."

The family accounts. His mother saw the published photograph and thought it resembled her son; his father agreed and believed the rifle "matched a rifle that was given to his son as a gift." On the State's account "Robinson implied that he was the shooter" and, asked why, "explained there is too much evil and the guy [Charlie Kirk] spreads too much hate."

Argument I — KGRD, the sole pleaded aggravator (the held Information independently confirms the circumstance is singular, §4): the State must show more than a "possibility" that another may be killed — a "high probability" — and that the defendant knew of it; the court may draw reasonable inferences but "may not speculate" (State v. Murphy, 2026 UT App 38; State v. Prisbrey). The brief adds that no limiting order caused the shortfall: no evidence excluded, no proffered expert excluded, no time limit imposed.

Argument II — Count 6 (tampering with a witness — directing the roommate to stay silent if questioned): the advice was "purely altruistic" and therefore not criminal, invoking United States v. Peterson, 385 F.3d 127 (2d Cir. 2004) for the proposition that the inducer's motive separates obstruction from altruistic advice, and framing the message as an invocation of the Fifth Amendment rights to counsel and to silence.

Argument III — Count 7 (offence in the presence of a child): the State's video showed two children present, but no evidence the shooter knew any child was present — the inference drawn from an alleged earlier campus walking tour is characterised as speculation (≈400 feet; a 35–44 second window). The brief asks that the parallel presence-of-a-child aggravating factor pleaded with Counts 1 and 2 be stricken for the same want of knowledge, and argues in the alternative against the State's backup position that enhancements need no proof at a preliminary hearing (Apprendi).

The court made no ruling on the scientific reliability of any DNA evidence — a Rule 702 question — which was litigated at length across the five evidentiary days and never decided (CR-E06 §2.9, DNA-E01 §8.3).
